note: The campsite is the back of the Refuge Trail parking area, the Martin Hill ATV trailhead on Blankley Road: a gravel-and-grass clearing about 35 m across, some 45 m off the road on a short spur, with a fire ring and a hitching post. During the summer ATV season (the Friday before Memorial Day to the last full weekend of September) the lot is used for unloading and riding, so expect trailers and machine noise; outside it the lot is quiet. Any camper may book it. Blankley Road is a forest road that leaves PA 326 at the mountain-summit ATV lot; the trailhead is 0.7 mile past the Y where Martin Hill Road splits off. Pack out trash. State forest roads are not plowed in winter. --Claude
summary: Site page re-read: CV013 still listed and bookable online, Drive-In, RV/Tent/Trailer categories, 60 ft, back-in gravel. It is the campsite at the back of DCNR's Refuge Trail ATV parking area (Martin Hill ATV trail): OHV staging, kept, fact in the note, owner question flagged. Fees confirmed, $6.50 reservation fee added; booking/hookups/season confirmed; pull_through false; facilities none. Imagery: clearing ~35 m across with the pin in it. NHD: unnamed stream 127 m (page: '400 feet from a stream').
flags: OHV STAGING - keep-or-drop question for the owner: site text 'Located on Blankley Road, Bedford at the Refuge Trail and Martin Hill ATV Trailhead. Gravel and grass ATV parking lot has a campsite at the back of it that will hold 1 camper trailer or 2 vehicles with tents. Easy access but visible from the roadway. Ideal for ATV riding during the summer riding season. Site has fire ring and hitching post. Potential site for equestrian use.' DCNR's Martin Hill ATV Trail brochure lists 'Refuge Trail Parking Area GPS: 39 51 29.4 N, 78 32 40.4 W ... ATV lot is 0.7 miles on the left' = 39.85817,-78.54456, 18 m from the site point. So it is a campsite inside an ATV trailhead lot, not an ordinary site near a trail. Nothing on the page restricts it to ATV riders (unlike Susquehannock's summer ATV-only sites), and the calendar sells it to anyone. Kept, with the fact in the note. DCNR: 'Designated ATV trails on state forest lands are open from the Friday before Memorial Day through the last full weekend in September'; some reopen in winter with the snowmobile season.
Horse use: 'Horse Hitching Post: Y', 'Potential site for equestrian use' - not equestrian-only.
Waterfront: stays not waterfront (NHD flowline 127 m; page '400 feet from a stream').
